competition.name: siim-isic-melanoma-classification
competition.description: Identify melanoma in lesion images. Predict the probability (`target`) that each skin lesion image in the test set is malignant, using the image plus patient-level metadata (age, sex, anatomical site).
competition.notes: MLE-bench medium-complexity split (prepared data from mle-bench, graded offline against private split). Large image dataset (DICOM + JPEG); heavy class imbalance (~1.8% positive). GPU strongly recommended.

grading.note: offline grade record(s) — graded against a held-out split, not a live leaderboard; see competition config notes for grading context

sections.siim-isic-melanoma-classification — run2:
**Final CV (ROC-AUC): 0.93214** — honest leave-fold-out score of a 6-member convex rank blend
(vit_small @384/256/320 px + efficientnet_b0 + CatBoost/LightGBM on metadata & image statistics).
Optimistic full-OOF counterpart 0.93291; patient-grouped cross-check 0.93278; best solo 0.92596
(vit_small @384 px). Deliverable: `submission.csv`, 4,142 rows, id order verified against
`sample_submission.csv`. Run wall time ~6.5 h, all training in the foreground.

---
sections.1. What was run:
Fresh run2. Everything from the earlier run was moved to `run1_archive/` before starting and was
not consulted for any modelling decision; the image caches were rebuilt from `data/jpeg` by this
run's own `scripts/prep_images.py`.

| Stage | Output |
|---|---|
| 0.5 Problem dossier | `dossier.json` |
| 1 EDA | `scripts/eda.py`, `eda_summary.json`, `cache/{train,test}_sizes.csv` |
| 2 Features | `scripts/prep_images.py` (pixels + image statistics), `scripts/common.py` (`build_features`) |
| 3 Modelling | `scripts/train_meta.py`, `scripts/discover.py`, `scripts/vision.py`, `scripts/finetune.py` |
| 4 Evaluation / blend | `scripts/blend.py`, `scripts/stack.py`, `blend_results.json` |
| 5 Submission | `scripts/submit.py`, `submission.csv` |

All 20 experiments are in `experiments.json` via `experiment_log.log_experiment_v2()`.
sections.2. The decision that mattered: the split:
The real SIIM-ISIC competition has patient-disjoint train/test, which makes
`StratifiedGroupKFold(patient_id)` the reflexive choice. **That reflex is wrong here.** EDA found
that mle-bench re-split the original 33,126-image train set **randomly by image** into
28,984 / 4,142:

- all **1,457** test patients also appear in train (overlap 1457/1457, 599 patients train-only);
- per-patient test share mean 0.124, median 0.111, vs an overall test share of 0.125.

So the graded test set is iid-by-image. A patient-grouped CV would have been measuring a strictly
harder problem than the one being scored. Primary CV is therefore `StratifiedKFold(5, seed=42)`
on images; every model additionally reports a patient-grouped `StratifiedGroupKFold` score as an
honesty check and as a leakage detector.

**The two agreed everywhere** — the largest gap across all 10 members was 0.0004 AUC
(blend 0.93214 image-level vs 0.93278 patient-grouped). That is a useful negative result: no
member is exploiting patient identity, so the choice cost nothing here. The one-line overlap
check remains worth doing every time.
sections.3. Results:
### Metadata + image-statistic models (no CNN)
Colour/texture statistics are computed for free during JPEG decoding (central-disc "lesion" vs
outer-ring "skin" colour, contrast, gradient energy, vignetting), plus resolution and
patient-relative "ugly duckling" z-scores.

| model | CV AUC | patient-grouped |
|---|---|---|
| LogisticRegression, sex+age+site only | 0.67148 | 0.67121 |
| LogisticRegression, all 54 features | 0.85467 | 0.85418 |
| LightGBM | 0.88574 | 0.88556 |
| XGBoost | 0.88668 | 0.88633 |
| **CatBoost** | **0.89171** | 0.89157 |

Feature-block ablation (LightGBM, identical folds, vs 0.88574 full):

| removed block | CV AUC | Δ |
|---|---|---|
| image colour/texture statistics | 0.82114 | **−0.06460** |
| image resolution | 0.87158 | −0.01417 |
| patient-relative (ugly duckling) | 0.87244 | −0.01330 |

The cheap image statistics are by far the largest tabular lever, and `ud_*` patient-relative
z-scores occupy 8 of the top-20 LightGBM importances — the clinical "ugly duckling" sign
(a lesion is suspicious *relative to that patient's other moles*) shows up directly in the model.

### Vision — discovery sweep (fold 0, 2 epochs, 256 px, 18 configs, 52 min)
Per-backbone LR mini-sweep, as `knowledge/vision_experience.md` requires:

| backbone | 1e-4 | 3e-4 | 1e-3 | best |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| vit_small_patch16_224 | **0.8853** | 0.8686 | 0.8173 | 1e-4 |
| efficientnet_b0 | 0.7686 | 0.8231 | **0.8782** | 1e-3 |
| efficientnet_b3 | 0.7868 | 0.8489 | **0.8716** | 1e-3 |
| resnet50 | 0.7608 | 0.8393 | **0.8694** | 1e-3 |
| resnet18 | 0.7936 | **0.8672** | 0.8551 | 3e-4 |
| convnext_tiny | **0.8643** | 0.8468 | 0.7775 | 1e-4 |

CNNs peak at 1e-3, ViT/ConvNeXt at 1e-4 — the pattern now holds on a 5th domain.

### Vision — full 5-fold fine-tunes (bf16, dihedral aug, 4× flip TTA, no class weighting)

| tag | backbone | px | ep | CV AUC | patient-grouped | wall |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| vit_small_384 | vit_small_patch16_224 | 384 | 8 | **0.92596** | 0.92589 | 89 min |
| vit_small_256 | vit_small_patch16_224 | 256 | 10 | 0.92309 | 0.92295 | 49 min |
| vit_small_320 | vit_small_patch16_224 (seed 2024) | 320 | 9 | 0.92024 | 0.92007 | 69 min |
| resnet50_256 | resnet50 | 256 | 10 | 0.89166 | 0.89179 | 70 min |
| effb0_256 | efficientnet_b0 | 256 | 10 | 0.88447 | 0.88440 | 48 min |

### Blend (Stage 4)
Rank-transform each member, then Caruana greedy selection with replacement. Reported score is the
**leave-fold-out** estimate: weights are refitted on 4 folds and scored on the held-out fold.

| | AUC |
|---|---|
| best solo (vit_small_384) | 0.92596 |
| equal weight, 10 members | 0.92517 |
| **optimised, full OOF (optimistic)** | 0.93291 |
| **leave-fold-out (honest — reported CV)** | **0.93214** |
| patient-grouped cross-check | 0.93278 |

Weights: vit_small_384 0.388, vit_small_256 0.286, vit_small_320 0.102, lgb_meta 0.102,
cat_meta 0.082, effb0_256 0.041. `resnet50_256`, `xgb_meta`, `lr_allfeat` and the level-2 stack
were given zero weight.
sections.4. What did not work:
- **A level-2 LightGBM stack lost to the convex blend.** Stacking member ranks together with
  context features (age, site, resolution, patient size) scored 0.92566 solo and earned ~0.02
  weight before being dropped entirely once vit_small_320 joined. Same direction as the s3e14
  Ridge-stacking counterexample in `knowledge/experience.md`.
- **Extra CNN families bought nothing.** Member-set comparison on the honest score:
  {vit384, vit256, 3× metadata} = 0.93204; + resnet50 = 0.93204; all 10 members = 0.93203. Both
  CNNs were zero-weighted or near-zero despite resnet50's respectable 0.89166 solo. Architecture
  diversity is not automatically useful; **input-resolution** diversity within the ViT family was,
  taking 0.78 of the total weight across three scales.
- **The discovery-scale gap widened rather than shrank.** vit_small led efficientnet_b0 by 0.007
  at 2 epochs and by 0.039 at 10 epochs — a direct counterexample to the digit-recognizer prior
  "don't over-prune on discovery scores". Both have been written back to the vision library.
sections.5. Tree search: deliberately not used —:
The skill designates tree search as the preferred Stage 4 loop *"where the budget justifies it"*,
and `references/07_tree_search.md` names the exact fallback that applies here: *"tiny data /
extremely expensive evaluation, where a ~60-node budget is unaffordable."*

A solo node in this competition is a 5-fold CNN fine-tune costing **48–89 min**. The prescribed
60-node budget is therefore **50–90 GPU-hours** against a ~8 h budget — two orders of magnitude
over. Spending the budget instead on one LR sweep plus five full fine-tunes was the right trade:
the single largest gain in the run (+0.037 AUC, metadata 0.892 → vit_small 0.926) came from
training a strong backbone at all, which no amount of node-space search over cheap models reaches.

Tree search restricted to the *blend layer* (nodes = member subsets and weights, seconds each) was
considered and rejected as redundant: with 10 members the greedy-with-replacement search already
covers that space, and the member-set comparison in §4 shows the blend is saturated — three
structurally different member sets land within 0.00001 of each other.
sections.6. Reproducibility:
Seeds fixed (`SEED=42`; vit_small_320 deliberately uses 2024 for decorrelation), folds persisted
to `cache/r2_folds.csv` and shared by every model so all scores are digit-for-digit comparable.
`torch.manual_seed` / `cuda.manual_seed_all` / `np.random.seed` are set per fold; cuDNN benchmark
is on (autotuning is not bit-deterministic across runs — a deliberate speed trade, and the
consequence is that CNN OOFs reproduce to ~1e-3 AUC, not bitwise).

Order: `prep_images.py 256` → `prep_images.py 384` → `prep_images.py 320` → `eda.py` →
`train_meta.py` → `discover.py` → `finetune.py <backbone> <lr> <px> <ep> <bs> <tag>` ×5 →
`stack.py` → `blend.py` → `submit.py blend`.
sections.7. Not submitted to Kaggle:
This is an offline mle-bench lane graded against the held-out private split; no Kaggle upload was
made and none was authorised. `submission.csv` is the deliverable.

texts.headless_run2.log:
Run complete, ~6.5 h, everything foreground.

## Result

**Final CV ROC-AUC 0.93214** (honest leave-fold-out of the convex rank blend). Best solo 0.92596 — `vit_small_patch16_224` @384px. `submission.csv`: 4,142 rows, id order verified against `sample_submission.csv`.

## Decision that mattered

EDA refuted the dossier's split hypothesis. The real SIIM competition is patient-disjoint; **mle-bench re-split the original 33,126 images randomly by image**, so all 1,457 test patients also appear in train (per-patient test share 0.124 vs overall 0.125). `StratifiedGroupKFold(patient_id)` would have measured a harder problem than the graded one. Primary CV = image-level `StratifiedKFold`; patient-grouped reported alongside as a leakage detector — the two agreed within 0.0004 AUC for all 10 members, so no member exploits patient identity.

## Pipeline

| stage | result |
|---|---|
| metadata + image stats | CatBoost 0.89171; ablation: image stats −0.065, resolution −0.014, ugly-duckling −0.013 |
| discovery (18 configs, 52 min) | CNNs peak 1e-3, ViT/ConvNeXt 1e-4 — 5th domain confirming this |
| 5 full fine-tunes | vit_small 384 **0.92596** / 256 0.92309 / 320 0.92024; resnet50 0.89166; effb0 0.88447 |
| blend | equal 0.92517, optimised 0.93291, **leave-fold-out 0.93214** |

## Negative results

- **Resolution diversity beat architecture diversity.** Three vit_small scales took 0.78 of blend weight; resnet50 and effb0 got ~0. Three structurally different member sets land within 0.00001.
- **Discovery-scale gap widened** (0.007 at 2ep → 0.039 at 10ep), contradicting the digit-recognizer prior "don't over-prune on discovery scores".
- **LGB level-2 stack lost to the convex blend** (0.92566 vs 0.93214) — same direction as the s3e14 Ridge-stacking counterexample.

## Tree search skipped — stated in STATUS.md §5

A solo node here is a 5-fold CNN fine-tune costing 48–89 min, so the prescribed 60-node budget is 50–90 GPU-hours against ~8 h. This is exactly the reference's own documented fallback ("extremely expensive evaluation"). Blend-layer-only tree search was rejected as redundant given the saturation evidence.

25 experiments logged via `log_experiment_v2()`; insights written back to `knowledge/experience.md` and `knowledge/vision_experience.md`; `dossier.json` carries the `eda_verdict`. Run1 outputs archived to `run1_archive/` and not used for any modelling decision.

One honest gap: dihedral augmentation was adopted but never ablated against no-aug, so its contribution is unmeasured.

dossier.json.run: run2 (fresh, 2026-07-29). run1 outputs archived under run1_archive/ and not consulted for modelling decisions.
dossier.json.task_family: image binary classification (dermoscopy) + patient-level tabular metadata

test_window.relation: iid-by-patient (hypothesis: disjoint patient groups, no temporal ordering)
test_window.evidence: no date column in train.csv/test.csv; patient_id present in both; mle-bench prepared split. Stage 1 EDA must check patient_id intersection train vs test.

split_policy.forbidden: plain StratifiedKFold — the same patient contributes many images (dermoscopy series), so a random split leaks patient-specific appearance into validation and inflates AUC
split_policy.rationale: grouping is the single most consequential CV decision here; AUC on a leaky split is optimistic without bound

metric.name: ROC-AUC
traps: pure ranking metric: class-imbalance reweighting (scale_pos_weight / is_unbalance) perturbs the loss surface without improving ranking — experience.md ROC-AUC section, validated on s3e3 / s4e1 / s6e2
no threshold/calibration needed; submit raw scores
1.76% positive rate means per-fold AUC variance is large — judge on pooled OOF, not per-fold

external_data.reason: config.yaml special_rules.external_data_allowed = false. Pretrained ImageNet backbones ARE allowed (pretrained_models_allowed = true) and are the main source of injected prior knowledge.

matched_task_priors: TASK-IMBALANCED [GEN] — positive rate ~1.8%: stratified folds, rank metric needs no resampling
TASK-BLEND-DECOR — plan a diverse-library decorrelating member (metadata GBDT) alongside the variance-heavy CNN members
matched_vision_experience: Per-backbone LR mini-sweep is mandatory before judging a backbone (a single fixed LR measures LR tolerance, not backbone quality)
Backbone ranking is DOMAIN-SPECIFIC — rediscover on dermoscopy, do not assume the digits/cifar/flowers winners
No multi-worker DataLoader (CUDA-fork deadlock hazard) — preload uint8 arrays, do resize/aug/normalise on GPU in batch
3-family convex blend on real OOFs beats best solo and equal weights in all 4 prior vision runs

data_level: dermoscopy lesions are orientation-free: h-flip + v-flip + 90-degree rotation are label-preserving (contrast: digits, where h-flip is forbidden). Expect a real gain, unlike cifar.
colour/contrast jitter: dermoscope hardware differs across contributing sites; jitter should reduce site-specific overfitting
raw image resolution (width x height) is a site/scanner fingerprint. It IS predictive but is a dataset artefact — treat as a candidate feature and ablate it explicitly rather than trusting it
patient-level context: a lesion is judged relative to the patient's other moles ('ugly duckling' sign) — per-patient normalised image statistics and patient image count are principled features
model_level: no class weighting (AUC is a ranking metric)
rank-average before blending (members have very different score scales)
TTA (flips) at inference — free variance reduction for a flip-invariant domain
convex weight search on OOF with a leave-fold-out honest estimate of the blend score

not_recorded: whether mle-bench's private split shares patients with the public test split — unobservable from here

eda_verdict.test_window.relation: REFUTED. The dossier hypothesised patient-disjoint groups (as in the real competition). EDA found the opposite: mle-bench re-split the original 33,126-image train set randomly BY IMAGE. All 1457 test patients also occur in train (overlap 1457/1457, 599 patients train-only); per-patient test share mean 0.124 / median 0.111 vs overall 0.125.
eda_verdict.split_policy: REVISED. Primary CV switched from StratifiedGroupKFold(patient_id) to StratifiedKFold(5) on images, which is regime-matched to the graded split. The grouped scheme is retained as a secondary honesty/leakage check and is reported for every model.
eda_verdict.split_policy_consequence: NULL in score terms: image-level and patient-grouped AUC agreed to within 0.0004 for all 10 members (blend 0.93214 vs 0.93278), i.e. no member exploits patient identity. The check is still mandatory — it was cheap and the failure mode is real.
eda_verdict.external_data.needed: CONFIRMED no. Pretrained ImageNet backbones (permitted) supplied all the injected prior knowledge; they are worth +0.037 AUC over the best tabular model.
eda_verdict.metric.traps: CONFIRMED. No class weighting was used anywhere; per-fold AUC spread is wide (e.g. effb0 0.873-0.910 across folds at ~103 positives per fold), so all decisions were taken on pooled OOF, never per-fold.

injection_ideas.data_level.dihedral augmentation: ADOPTED (h-flip + v-flip + transpose + 4x flip TTA); not ablated against no-aug, so the size of its contribution is not measured — an honest gap.
injection_ideas.data_level.resolution as scanner fingerprint: CONFIRMED predictive and it transfers: dropping the resolution block costs -0.014 AUC, and the train/test resolution distributions match closely (6000x4000 = 44.5% of train vs 43.9% of test).
injection_ideas.data_level.ugly duckling / patient-relative stats: CONFIRMED, the strongest single idea in the dossier: -0.013 AUC when removed, and 8 of the top-20 LightGBM importances are ud_* columns.
injection_ideas.data_level.image colour/texture statistics: CONFIRMED and understated in the dossier: the largest tabular block at -0.065 AUC when removed.

eda_verdict.injection_ideas.model_level: All adopted (no class weighting, rank-average before blending, flip TTA, convex weights with a leave-fold-out honest estimate).
